title: Smooth connected commutative exponent-p groups over a perfect field are vector groups
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. All groups are affine $k$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and subgroups are closed subgroup schemes [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Smoothness and connectedness mean [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme]. Assume $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$ and every element of $k$ is a $p$-th power. Let $G$ be smooth, connected and commutative. Suppose $[p]_G=0$, meaning that the sum of $p$ copies of every $g\in G(R)$ is zero for every commutative $k$-algebra $R$. Then for some integer $d\geq0$ there is an isomorphism of $k$-group schemes $\mathbf G_a^d\xrightarrow{\sim}G$. Here $\mathbf G_a(R)=(R,+)$ for every commutative $k$-algebra $R$ [def-sc-gm-ga], and $\mathbf G_a^0$ is the trivial group $1=\operatorname{Spec}k$.

source.place: Proposition 14.54, printed p.297 (also Proposition 14.49 and Corollary 14.53).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-p-torsion-additive-embedding] to $G$: the hypotheses are precisely smoothness, commutativity, finite type, affineness and $[p]_G=0$. Obtain a closed embedding $G\hookrightarrow\mathbf G_a^n$.

source.place: Proposition 14.49, printed p.296; first sentence of Proposition 14.54, printed p.297.

proof.text: The field hypothesis says exactly that $k$ is perfect in characteristic $p$. Apply [lem-sfb-additive-subgroup-perfect-decomposition] to the closed subgroup of step 1, obtaining an isomorphism $b:G\simeq\mathbf G_a^d\times\prod_{j=1}^s\alpha_{p^{r_j}}\times E$, with all $r_j\geq1$ and $E$ finite etale.

By [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced], applied to $G\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, $G$ is reduced. If an $\alpha_{p^{r_j}}$ factor occurred, its projection would have a section by setting all other coordinates equal to their identities. Thus $k[t]/(t^{p^{r_j}})\to\mathcal O(G)$ would have a left inverse and be injective. The nonzero nilpotent class of $t$ would remain nonzero and nilpotent, contradicting reducedness. Hence $s=0$.

source.place: Corollary 14.53, printed p.297: exclusion of infinitesimal factors; geometric reducedness input Stacks Tag 056T, varieties.tex lemma-smooth-geometrically-normal.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-over-field-product] to $C=\mathcal O(E)$: $C\simeq\prod_{i=1}^m L_i$ with finite separable fields $L_i/k$. The identity $C\to k$ shows $m>0$. If $m>1$, a nontrivial coordinate idempotent stays nontrivial in $\mathcal O(G)$: the projection $G\simeq\mathbf G_a^d\times E\to E$ has the zero-coordinate section, so its ring map is injective. Its two principal opens $D(e),D(1-e)$ are nonempty, disjoint, and cover $G$, contradicting [def-weil-connected-scheme]. Thus $C=L_1$. The identity map $L_1\to k$ is injective and its image contains $k$, hence is a $k$-algebra isomorphism. Therefore $E=\operatorname{Spec}k$ is the trivial group. Invert the resulting group isomorphism $b:G\simeq\mathbf G_a^d$ to get the requested arrow, including $d=0$.

source.place: Corollary 14.53, printed p.297: exclusion of etale factors. Field-product input: Stacks Tag 00U3, algebra.tex lemma-etale-over-field.
